page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 instruction set. It provisions 56 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 28 physical processor cores with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 224 GB, allocating 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported natively alongside standard AVX, whereas AVX-512 and AMX vector extensions are not present. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmarking demonstrates competitive performance across heavily multi-threaded CPU tasks. The instance achieved top-quartile results in Geekbench multi-core evaluations (17,030.0) and PassMark CPU scoring (63,148.67), bolstered by high execution efficiency in Clang software compilation and ray tracing. In memory metrics, PassMark scores landed in the top 10%, complemented by 3,877.36 GB/sec in small-block cached read throughput, though uncached large-block throughput remained within median ranges. Text generation inference for small and mid-sized language models registered strong output speeds, showing viable CPU-only inferencing performance for compact models.

From an architectural perspective, the instance balances broad core scaling against moderate single-thread frequency, evidenced by average Geekbench single-core and compression marks. The absence of native NVMe storage requires external persistent disks, shifting I/O economics onto network-attached storage performance. However, its high vCPU and RAM density provides cost-effective throughput for parallelized execution where hardware acceleration is unnecessary. The c2d-standard-56 is well matched for continuous integration build farms, distributed batch simulations, large-scale software compilation, ray tracing rendering, and CPU-driven inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 56 dedicated virtual CPUs across 28 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading, paired with 224 GB of system memory at a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not included, requiring external disk volumes for persistent state, and no discrete GPUs are bundled. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates upper-quartile multi-core compute throughput, excelling in PassMark CPU tests, Clang software builds, and ray tracing. Memory subsystems deliver top-decile PassMark memory scores alongside strong small-block cached read bandwidth. The c2d-standard-56 delivers robust compute density per resource unit, making it an efficient choice for large-scale software compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference, and high-throughput batch processing pipelines.
